quirks: Requires a valid `ref` for a Postgres project OWNED BY THE CALLING WALLET — access is wallet-scoped, you can only query projects your own wallet created.
No standalone ref exists: you must first POST /api/stablebase/projects/create ($1.00) to provision a DB and get a ref, OR POST /api/stablebase/projects/list ({}, $0.01) to find an existing one.
Master wallet currently owns ZERO projects (projects/list returned []), so this query endpoint could not be exercised with a real ref.
The PAYING wallet must match the owning wallet — querying with a ref owned by a different wallet will be rejected.
Guessing/fabricating a ref will 404 and waste the $0.02 payment.
usage.guide: Stablebase query runs SQL against a serverless Postgres project that YOUR wallet owns. Before calling, obtain a `ref`: either provision one via POST https://stablebase.dev/api/stablebase/projects/create ($1.00, body {name, db_pass, region}) or find an existing owned one via POST https://stablebase.dev/api/stablebase/projects/list ({}, $0.01). Then POST https://stablebase.dev/api/stablebase/database/query with {ref, query} ($0.02) and read the returned rows from the JSON body. Access is wallet-scoped, so the wallet that pays for the query must be the same one that created the project; a foreign or fake ref fails.
